premises.text: FluidDB is a shared writable database so related app data need not live in unrelated silos
premises.evidence_span: applications that had related data no longer were forced to store it into unrelated databases

premises.text: Independent apps writing to FluidDB enable unanticipated combined queries without mutual awareness
premises.evidence_span: I've combined data in an unanticipated way from three independent but related applications. And those applications are not aware of each other. They have no knowledge of each other

premises.text: Anyone can add information to anything without permission on shared writable objects for everything
premises.evidence_span: any person or any application can come along and add information to anything without asking for permission

value.text: Information stored together is more valuable because it is more useful
value.evidence_span: store their information into a place that makes it more valuable, because it's more useful

secondary_value.text: Data is social — related information lives in the same place
secondary_value.evidence_span: It's one in which data is social. where information that is related lives in the same place

causal_links.evidence_span: makes it more valuable, because it's more useful

notes: One-domain theory. Permissionless write + shared objects merged as one writable-platform condition. Soft count at 3.
